transcript.text: Hi, the light in my Neff oven has stopped working (model B1ACE4HN0B). Oven works fine otherwise. Can I change the bulb myself and what bulb do I need?

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. Yes, you can probably change the bulb yourself. It is a standard owner-safe repair on most Neff ovens. The bulb you need is a 300°C heat-resistant oven lamp, typically with an SES (small Edison screw) or E14 fitting and around 25 watts. You do not need to buy a branded 'Neff' part; any standard high-temperature appliance bulb from a DIY store will work fine. Is there a clear glass cover over the bulb? If so, does it unscrew or clip off? This determines how easy it is to reach and whether you need to handle any screws.

Thanks. I'll isolate it at the cooker switch and let it cool first. Yes, there's a glass cover and it twists off - I got it off using a rubber glove for grip. The old bulb says E14, 25W, 300C and the filament looks broken.

That suggests it is just a blown bulb. The broken filament means the circuit is open and the light cannot work. 1. 2. Unscrew the old E14 300°C heat-resistant bulb from the holder.
3. Screw in a new standard SES/E14 25W (or similar wattage, e.g., up to 40W if specified by the manufacturer, but 25W is typical for Neff) oven-rated bulb. Do not touch the glass of the new bulb with bare fingers; use a cloth or wear gloves, as skin oils can cause it to crack when hot.
4. Screw the glass cover back on until snug.
5. Turn the power back on and test. If the light does not come on with a known-good bulb, then the issue is likely the lamp holder or its wiring, which would require an engineer. Otherwise, you are all set.
